domain_title: Purpose, value, context, roles and classification
title: AI suitability, proportionality and value hypothesis
canonical_definition: A2 evaluates whether AI is suitable and proportionate for a defined problem: the organization records the current process, affected users, and a measurable improvement over a non-AI baseline before committing to an AI approach, and compares expected benefit with total cost, operating effort, human impact, and risk.
governance_purpose: Ensure AI investment and use are justified by a specific, measurable and falsifiable value case that remains proportionate to alternatives, total cost, operational burden, human impact and risk.
distinct_claim: A1 defines the intended use boundary; A2 evaluates whether the AI intervention is justified and proportionate within that boundary; A5 governs the lifecycle transition decision informed by A2 evidence; paired AP-A2 is evaluated independently.

conditions: Applies to all proposed and materially changed AI uses across internal, procured, and embedded capabilities; assessment depth scales with autonomy, affected-person exposure, cost, operational dependency, and reversibility.
No blanket exemption applies merely because an AI feature is embedded, pre-licensed, low-cost, or labeled experimental.
ISOLATED_SANDBOX and CONTROLLED_PILOT are operating-boundary environments, not lifecycle stages; progression from pilot to production requires evidenced value and proportionality verification.

primary_questions.question: Is the problem, desired outcome and measurable value hypothesis defined independently of the AI solution?
Has the chosen AI approach been compared with simpler alternatives and implemented with explicit cost-risk trade-offs?
Do representative trials show sufficient value and feasibility to justify progression, with stop criteria applied?

atomic_subcriteria.criterion: The underlying problem, affected process or decision and desired outcome are defined independently of AI technology, vendor or model capability.
A current technology-neutral baseline and relevant counterfactual define what improvement must be demonstrated.
The value hypothesis uses outcome measures, owners, thresholds, time horizons and falsification conditions rather than activity or model metrics alone.
Feasible non-AI, deterministic, process, data, human-service and no-change alternatives are compared using explicit criteria.
The selected approach is proportionate after considering benefit, consequence, uncertainty, rights and human impact, total cost, complexity and control burden.
Implementation includes measurable budgets, resource and human-work controls, ownership and traceability for assumptions used in the value case.
Representative comparative trials test the current solution against the approved baseline and alternatives using pre-defined metrics and thresholds.
Continuation, stop, constraint and scale criteria are applied to the complete evidence, including negative, subgroup, cost and risk results.
Operational evidence monitors realized value, cost, quality, human workload and impact and triggers requalification after material deviation or change.

capability_indicators: Value metrics and owners are named
Cost and operational consequences are considered
Continuation and stop criteria are enforced

required_evidence.title: Technology-neutral problem and outcome baseline
required_evidence.description: The organization has defined the problem, affected process, desired outcome and current baseline independently of a predetermined AI solution. Acceptance: Defines the current process or decision, users and affected persons, baseline performance, constraints and desired outcome. Uses language that remains meaningful if AI is removed from the proposed solution. Boundary: A use-case title, vendor proposal or model capability statement does not establish a problem baseline.

required_evidence.title: Measurable value hypothesis and ownership record
required_evidence.description: Expected benefit is expressed as measurable outcomes with owners, thresholds, time horizons and causal assumptions. Acceptance: Separates business, user, societal and operational outcomes from activity, usage and model metrics. Identifies baseline, target, measurement method, owner, decision date and conditions that would falsify the hypothesis. Boundary: Adoption, prompt volume, feature delivery or benchmark improvement alone does not establish realized value.

required_evidence.title: Alternative and proportionality assessment
required_evidence.description: The selected AI approach has been compared with feasible simpler, non-AI and lower-risk alternatives using explicit decision criteria. Acceptance: Considers process change, rules, deterministic automation, analytics, data improvement, human service and no-change options where feasible. Explains why the selected mechanism is proportionate to expected benefit, consequence, uncertainty, cost and control burden. Boundary: A vendor shortlist or comparison between AI models is not a complete alternatives assessment.

required_evidence.title: Total cost and resource baseline
required_evidence.description: Build, buy, integration, evaluation, security, governance, operations, monitoring, human review, incident and exit costs are identified and bounded. Acceptance: Includes variable usage, model/provider, data, infrastructure, people, assurance and change costs for the target scale. Records assumptions, sensitivity ranges, budget owner and cost thresholds. Boundary: Prototype API cost or licence price alone cannot establish total cost of ownership.

required_evidence.title: Risk, impact and control-burden assessment
required_evidence.description: Expected benefit is evaluated alongside foreseeable harms, uncertainty, dependency, human impact and required governance controls. Acceptance: Uses the same system, scope, lifecycle and affected-person boundary as the value hypothesis. Identifies whether required controls or human work materially reduce the proposed benefit or feasibility. Boundary: A generic risk register or low internal risk score does not establish proportionality.

required_evidence.title: Representative comparative trial results
required_evidence.description: Executed evaluation compares the current AI solution with the approved baseline and relevant alternatives under representative conditions. Acceptance: Defines versions, samples, users, operating conditions, metrics, thresholds, costs, failures and confidence limitations before interpreting results. Includes negative, neutral and subgroup results and does not exclude material failure modes. Boundary: A demonstration, benchmark, test plan or selected successful cases cannot establish comparative value.

required_evidence.title: Operational benefit and economics records
required_evidence.description: Current operation demonstrates whether expected value, cost, quality and human workload are realized within the approved boundary. Acceptance: Covers representative time periods, user groups, volumes, exception handling, human review, rework and downstream consequences. Reconciles realized outcomes and costs with the approved value hypothesis and baseline. Boundary: High usage or positive feedback without outcome and cost evidence does not establish realized value.

required_evidence.title: Continuation, stop and requalification decision record
required_evidence.description: Progression, continuation, constraint or termination follows pre-defined criteria and an attributable decision. Acceptance: Records evidence considered, threshold result, dissent, conditions, expiry, accountable authority and next reassessment point. Prevents sunk cost, schedule pressure or technical availability from silently overriding stop criteria. Boundary: A backlog decision, funding renewal or deployment event is not sufficient without the decision basis.

sufficiency: Compare outcomes on the same scope and workload against a dated non-AI baseline with named owners and pre-agreed thresholds.

Record UNKNOWN for the affected question when the baseline, alternatives analysis, or outcome evidence is missing or materially contradictory; record NOT_SATISFIED where verified evidence establishes a shortfall.
Use the current solution, model/provider version, operating boundary, scale and cost assumptions.
Repeat comparative assessment after material change or threshold breach.
Operational value evidence must cover a representative period and remain within the decision record expiry.
evidence_rules.evidence_ceiling: Problem and value-hypothesis statements establish DECLARED assurance only; alternatives matrices and cost models establish IMPLEMENTED design analysis, not TESTED effectiveness; executed representative trials establish TESTED assurance only for the evaluated system version and operating context.
false_positive_guards: Do not treat model benchmark scores, token/query volume, or slide-deck ROI projections as evidence of realized value or proportionality.
Do not treat a comparison solely between different LLM vendors as a technology-neutral alternatives assessment.
Do not treat the presence of AI as disproportionate solely because a simpler conceptual alternative exists; assess feasibility, outcome and total constraint.
Do not treat a high-cost solution as disproportionate when evidence shows commensurate value and controlled risk.
Do not treat early uncertainty as value theatre when the experiment has explicit falsifiable hypotheses, bounded exposure and enforced stop criteria.
Do not treat low adoption as failure without determining whether adoption is a valid causal requirement for the target outcome.
prohibited_inferences: Do not infer AP-A2 presence solely because A2 is NOT_SATISFIED or UNKNOWN.
Do not infer legal or regulatory compliance from satisfying A2.
Do not infer production value from an unconstrained prototype demo.
Do not infer value from model quality, user engagement, press visibility, innovation activity or delivery completion alone.
Do not infer proportionality from executive sponsorship, provider reputation or budget approval.
Do not infer that AI is required because the current manual process is weak.
Do not infer production readiness from a successful demonstration or average result that excludes material costs, harms or failure conditions.

conditions: Block consequential deployment when the problem, value hypothesis or proportionality rationale is materially undefined.
Block progression when representative evidence fails pre-defined minimum value, feasibility or risk thresholds and no formally approved constrained experiment remains.
Constrain operation when benefit, cost or human-impact evidence is materially incomplete for the proposed scale.
Stop or requalify continued use when approved stop criteria are met or the decision record has expired.

normative_source_mappings.relevant_locator: NIST AI 100-1 (January 2023) MAP 1.3 & MAP 1.4 (p. 31); MAP 3, MAP 3.1 & MAP 3.2 (p. 32); MANAGE 1.1, MANAGE 2.1, MANAGE 2.2 & MANAGE 2.4 (p. 37)
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: Voluntary risk-management guidance supporting organizational AI goals, business-value definition and re-evaluation, comparative benefit/cost examination against benchmarks, consideration of viable non-AI alternatives, and continuation/disengagement decisions.

finding_definitions.title: Problem, desired outcome or value hypothesis is not defined independently of the AI solution
Feasible alternatives and proportionality have not been credibly assessed
Total cost, resource demand, human workload or control burden is materially incomplete
Representative comparative evidence does not demonstrate sufficient value or feasibility
Continuation, stop or value-realization controls are not enforced
